svg.title: RIEMANN R2 — The proof, chapter by chapter: what each chapter of the blueprint proves, and which chapters use which
svg.desc: The blueprint reads Alpöge's formal proof as nine chapters: the main theorems, an outline, five chapters that each carry out one stage of the argument, and a chapter of published results. Each card is one chapter: the Lean declaration of the theorem it proves, the chapter's own introduction, its sections with the number of statements in each, and the chapters it uses. An arrow from A to B says that chapter B uses chapter A; read it from the foot up, as diagram R1. The table at the foot counts which published results the proof leans on most. No Lean was built for the blueprint; see band 5 of diagram R1 for what is known about the formal proof.

This chapter collects the published theorems that the proof uses, each in the form in which it is used. It is a catalogue and has no main theorem: the other chapters cite its entries in their proofs, never as hypotheses. None of these theorems is assumed. Each comes with a proof, which the entry sketches, though for many we only name what the proof draws on.

text.tspan: 5. Theta lifts, periods and the Siegel-Weil formula

svg.text: thm-theta-inputs has no Lean declaration: it is the blueprint's own grouping of the chapter's results

A member of a family in chap-families is a chain of definite unitary groups joined by theta lifts. To show that the families satisfy their conditions we need several facts about these lifts: that they do not
vanish, that they separate vectors, that suitable test vectors have algebraic values, how their norms depend on L-values, and how the periods built from them behave. This chapter proves these facts.
thm-theta-inputs collects them.
The Siegel-Weil formula (sec-theta-siegel-weil): 8 statements
Theta towers and their step identities (sec-theta-towers): 4 statements
Non-vanishing and separation of theta lifts (sec-theta-separation): 7 statements
Rational test vectors (sec-theta-test-vectors): 7 statements
L-values along Witt towers and the indefinite slope bound (sec-theta-witt): 4 statements
The isometric period identity (sec-theta-period-identity): 7 statements
Bessel transforms and archimedean models (sec-theta-bessel): 7 statements
The off-diagonal bound (sec-theta-offdiag): 8 statements
Counting automorphic forms and mass constants (sec-theta-counting): 4 statements
Valuations of periods and CM theta measures (sec-theta-valuations): 4 statements
Statements 61: 7 modified, 48 new, 5 published, 1 unlabelled

theorem galoisLocalGlobalStrong_recParameter : UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b recT

This chapter proves thm-galois-reps-polarized: every polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representation π of GL_a over a CM field has an l-adic Galois representation, with the Hodge–Tate weights read
off π and with Weil–Deligne representations that match the local parameters of π wherever these are determined (rem-local-parameters-weak). The outline needs it in thm-grh-from-galois: these
representations bound the Tate–Shafarevich groups of chap-sha and enter the families of chap-families. The statement is a weak form of the theorem of Harris–Taylor, Shin, Chenevier–Harris,
Barnet-Lamb–Gee–Geraghty–Taylor and Caraiani.
From odd rank and theta lifts to all polarized pairs (sec-gal-assembly): 3 statements

Geometric Galois representations in odd rank (sec-gal-odd-rank): 2 statements

theorem UpperTheory.One.vwin_of_row (h : UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b fun h rc => UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.IsRecT h rc) : UpperTheory.Top.VWin

This chapter proves thm-sha-bound and shows where the rest of the proof uses it. For a primitive Dirichlet character ψ the ψ-fields E are abelian fields in a 2-power cyclotomic tower (def-sha-bound). The theorem says that the Tate–Shafarevich groups Ш^1_l(E, e) of the Tate twists Q_l/Z_l(-e), 0 < e < t = ⌊

x^(401)⌋, are finite, and that the sum of their lengths, weighted by log l, is at most e^(x^ε/2). The families of definite unitary groups (chap-families) carry an error term that these lengths control, and the bound keeps that term small.
Second cohomology of Tate twists (sec-sha-h2): 2 statements
Selmer groups from Kato's Euler system (sec-sha-kato): 3 statements
Kato's explicit reciprocity law (sec-sha-reciprocity): 5 statements
Automorphy of symplectic lifts (sec-sha-gsp4): 5 statements
The error term of the families (sec-sha-error): 8 statements
Congruence modules and Selmer groups (sec-sha-congruence): 2 statements
Local lifting theorems for crystalline lattices (sec-sha-lifting): 8 statements
Uses chap-galois, chap-literature
Used by architecture, chap-families

This chapter proves thm-family-data-exists: if cuspidal representations of GL_a over CM fields have Galois representations, some class of families of definite unitary groups satisfies the family hypotheses. The zero-free region needs them: thm-zero-free-from-families takes such a class, together with the
Tate–Shafarevich bound, and shows that primitive Dirichlet L-functions have no zeros right of 1/2.

text.tspan: The five stages of the proof (the architecture chapter's own list)

svg.text: Galois representations (chap-galois). To every polarized regular algebraic cuspidal representation of GL_a over a CM field we attach a Galois representation, compatible with a weak form of the local
Langlands correspondence (thm-galois-reps-polarized).
The Tate–Shafarevich bound (chap-sha). These representations bound the Tate–Shafarevich groups of the twists Q_l/Z_l(-e) over the abelian fields that a Dirichlet character ψ cuts out of a 2-power
cyclotomic tower (thm-sha-bound).

Families (chap-families). For each primitive ψ and each large x, an auxiliary CM field of degree about x^2 carries families of definite unitary groups of growing rank, linked by theta lifts and carrying
hermitian lattices (thm-family-data-exists). The theta lifts and the Siegel–Weil formula (chap-theta) and a covolume bound from arithmetic heights (chap-heights) give the families their properties …

Slope data and the core inequality (chap-zero-free). The families give a slope inequality for the hermitian lattices at primes inert in the auxiliary field. Averaged along a chain of theta lifts, it bounds a
weighted von Mangoldt sum G_m(x) by x^(1/2 + O(ε)) (thm-core-inequality).
Landau's theorem (chap-zero-free). The bound holds on windows [Y, Y^(3/2)] of arbitrarily large Y, and Landau's theorem on Dirichlet series with non-negative coefficients turns it into a zero-free
half-plane (thm-landau-windows).

text.tspan: 3. From prime sums to the zero-free half-plane

svg.text: theorem zeroFreeAll_of_topG {la : ℝ} (hla : 1 < la) (h : TopG) (hS : ∀ ψ : PChar, HostExW la (GChi ψ).req) : ZeroFreeAll

This chapter proves thm-zero-free-from-connected: if families of definite unitary groups carry slope data, and auxiliary CM fields exist at every scale of long windows, then no primitive Dirichlet L-function vanishes right of the critical line. It is the analytic half of the proof. Other chapters supply the two hypotheses:
chap-families builds the families, and chap-sha proves the Tate–Shafarevich bound from which the auxiliary fields are made.
Landau's theorem on windows (sec-zf-windows): 4 statements
Auxiliary CM fields (sec-zf-auxiliary-fields): 3 statements
The core inequality (sec-zf-core): 4 statements
Slope data from families (sec-zf-slope-data): 5 statements
The local link at inert primes (sec-zf-local-link): 7 statements
Uses chap-families, chap-literature
Statements 24: 2 modified, 21 new, 1 published

text.tspan: Points to check first (the blueprint's own list,

svg.text: Writing this blueprint turned up statements that are weaker than their names suggest, or whose role we could not settle. None of them is an error we have found. They are where a careful reader should look
first.
Local and global compatibility.
The local parameters are not the local Langlands correspondence (rem-local-parameters-weak), and the Galois representations are compatible with them only where the parameter is determined (
def-galois-reps-polarized).
In odd rank, the geometric construction gives a representation of unknown dimension on which the Satake polynomial kills Frobenius (thm-geometric-galois-odd-rank). The transfer to Shimura varieties
cites no trace formula (thm-transfer-unitary-shimura).
The dual of an abelian scheme is asked to be a scheme over every base (thm-dual-abelian-scheme); classically it is in general only an algebraic space.
Steps with internal hypotheses. Some steps take as hypotheses results proved elsewhere in the argument. The slope bound on the indefinite side (thm-indefinite-slope-bound) uses five statements on
L-values, gathered in thm-non-endoscopic-hypotheses-hold. …
theorem UpperTheory.FinalTheorems.everyCharacter_of_row (h : UpperTheory.GalStar.Row0b fun h rc => UpperTheory.Zero.LLC.IsRecT h rc) : UpperTheory.EveryCharacter

This chapter sketches Alpöge's proof of thm-half-plane: no Dirichlet L-function vanishes for Re s > 1/2. The proof has an arithmetic half, which builds Galois representations and uses them to bound Tate–Shafarevich groups, and an analytic half, which turns that bound into a zero-free half-plane through families of
definite unitary groups. It runs in five stages, and each later chapter carries out one of them.
What the stages pass to each other (sec-outline-interfaces): 5 statements
From the Tate-Shafarevich bound to the half-plane (sec-outline-chain): 4 statements
Points to check (sec-outline-check): 1 statements
Uses chap-zero-free, chap-families, chap-sha, chap-galois
Statements 11: 2 modified, 6 new, 1 published, 2 unlabelled

Main theorem thm-grh-from-galois: GRH from Galois representations · Lean UpperTheory.FinalTheorems. everyCharacter_of_row at src/Development/ AutomorphicArithmetic/ CharacterBoxes/MainConclusion. lean:7
Blueprint architecture/
theorem LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re : DirichletLNonvanishingRightOfHalf

Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, and of the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions, has two steps. The hard step is a single statement: no Dirichlet L-function vanishes in the

half-plane Re s > 1/2 (thm-half-plane). The rest of this chapter derives the theorems about zeros on the critical line from it by the functional equation, an argument of a few lines. The remaining chapters
prove thm-half-plane.
No sections: the chapter is its statements.
Used by no other chapter: it states the results
Statements 8: 5 new, 3 published
Main theorem thm-half-plane: GRH, half-plane form · Lean LFunction_ne_zero_of_half_lt_re at src/Main.lean:8
